metadata.name: 经典电影片段
metadata.description: 经典英文电影名段独白：希望、梦想、勇气与自由

items.title: Forrest Gump (1994) / 阿甘正传
items.author: Robert Zemeckis (dir.), Eric Roth (screenplay)
items.content:
The 1994 film Forrest Gump, adapted from Winston Groom's novel, follows a simple-hearted Alabama man who runs through three decades of American history. Sitting on a park bench, he tells strangers the story of his life, which his mother taught him to face with calm.

One line from the film has become a household saying:

"Life is like a box of chocolates. You never know what you're gonna get."

items.title: The Shawshank Redemption (1994) / 肖申克的救赎
items.author: Frank Darabont (dir./screenplay), Stephen King (novella)
items.content:
Based on a Stephen King novella, this 1994 film tells how Andy Dufresne, a banker wrongly convicted of murder, spends nineteen years quietly digging his way to freedom — and how he keeps hope alive for his friend Red behind the prison walls.

Near the end, Andy writes to Red about the one thing prison cannot take away:

"Hope is a good thing, maybe the best of things, and no good thing ever dies."
items.source: The Shawshank Redemption (1994), Castle Rock Entertainment

items.title: The Pursuit of Happyness (2006) / 当幸福来敲门
items.author: Gabriele Muccino (dir.), Steve Conrad (screenplay)
items.content:
This 2006 drama is based on the true story of Chris Gardner, a homeless salesman who raises his young son alone while competing for an unpaid brokerage internship, until hardship finally turns into a career.

Playing basketball with his boy, he teaches him the lesson he himself lives by:

"You got a dream, you gotta protect it."
items.source: The Pursuit of Happyness (2006), Columbia Pictures

items.title: The Legend of 1900 (1998) / 海上钢琴师
items.author: Giuseppe Tornatore (dir.), Alessandro Baricco (monologue)
items.content:
In this 1998 Italian film, a pianist named 1900 is born aboard an ocean liner and never once steps ashore, playing music that captivates every passenger who crosses the Atlantic with him.

When his best friend urges him to leave the ship and see the world, he explains why he never will:

"Land is a ship too big for me."

items.title: Dead Poets Society (1989) / 死亡诗社
items.author: Peter Weir (dir.), Tom Schulman (screenplay)
items.content:
Set in a conservative American boarding school in 1959, this 1989 film follows John Keating, an unconventional English teacher who reopens his students' eyes to poetry and independent thought, and inspires them to revive a secret club called the Dead Poets Society.

He urges the boys to make the most of their brief lives:

"Carpe diem. Seize the day, boys."

items.title: Braveheart (1995) / 勇敢的心
items.author: Mel Gibson (dir.), Randall Wallace (screenplay)
items.content:
This 1995 epic portrays the Scottish knight William Wallace, who leads a revolt against English rule in the late thirteenth century and pays for freedom with his life.

Facing execution, he cries out words that echo through the story:

"They may take our lives, but they'll never take our freedom!"
